paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. God warns before He judges, and this whole passage is a warning. He tells Jerusalem, "Be forewarned, O Jerusalem, or I will turn away from you…" (Jeremiah 6:8). A warning is a mercy, because it means the door isn't shut yet.

So why was judgment coming? The LORD says, "from the least of them to the greatest, all are greedy for gain; from prophet to priest, all practice deceit" (Jeremiah 6:13). The ones who should have been telling the truth were saying, "Peace, peace," when there was no peace at all (Jeremiah 6:14). And Jeremiah says the word of the LORD had become offensive to them, and they found no pleasure in it (Jeremiah 6:10).

That part hits close to home, baker. It's easy to want the soft word, the tiny cartoon bandage, instead of the true one. This is a heavy passage, so let it sit. But the LORD's warnings are never the problem, and ears that stay closed are. So ask Him for ears that listen, and for a heart that can still blush, because He is the One who makes things new (Revelation 21:5).
